reference_product: AI pull-request review category: CodeRabbit, Greptile, GitHub Copilot code review, Qodo Merge / PR-Agent
target_platforms: GitHub App (GitLab P1, Azure DevOps/Bitbucket P2)
chosen_stack: LangGraph (Python) + FastAPI + LangGraph Server standalone container + PostgreSQL 16/pgvector + Redis 7 + S3-compatible storage + Next.js 15 + Stripe; models provider-abstracted with tiered adaptive routing, defaults Claude Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Haiku 4.5
open_decisions: D15 Whether 'Quorum' is the final product name (working title; keep for now, resolve trademark, domain, PR-thread identity and comprehension before GA)
D1 Default comment budget (8 proposed, tune from held-promotion rate after beta)
D2 Whether 'unprovable' findings may ever post (recommendation: never in MVP)
D3 Cross-provider verification as default or Business+ only
D4 Seat definition (active author+reviewer per period proposed)
D5 GitLab connector before or after auto-fix
D6 Whether the advisory style lane survives beta
D7 Vector storage for very large monorepos (pgvector until 5M chunks)
D8 How much of the benchmark corpora to publish
D9 Free-tier private repo allowance (1 proposed)
D10 Blocking checks never default (escalation only)
D11 Trace retention default (30 days proposed)
D12 Whether the verifier sees analyzer output (yes, static_tool evidence only)
Unresolved with data: optimal refute-rate band, per-repo vs per-org calibration threshold, real recall cost of the comment budget, per-lane yield justification
D13 Whether the routing policy is customer-tunable or vendor-managed (mode switch + escalation budget proposed for M6)
D14 Whether adaptive routing is on by default for new orgs (off at M6, revisit at M7)
Unresolved with data: which of the six escalation triggers earn their cost, and whether per-repo lane yield is a safe de-escalation signal or a cold-start trap
